name: Urogenital Tract Malformation

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Imaging Diagnostic Criteria for Urogenital Tract Malformations

criteria.description: Presence of structural abnormalities in the urogenital tract detected by imaging or surgery
Clinical evidence of impaired urinary function such as obstruction or incontinence
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes associated with urogenital development
Presence of associated congenital anomalies in related systems (e.g., renal or reproductive)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of at least two major criteria including documented structural abnormality and clinical urinary dysfunction
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis often requires multidisciplinary evaluation including imaging and genetic testing.

pathognomonic.notes: Commonly leads to urinary retention or hydronephrosis
Retrograde flow of urine from bladder to ureters/kidneys

searchTerms: fluid buildup in kidney before birth

common.notes: Secondary to urinary stasis or reflux
May be present in complex malformations
Due to structural or functional abnormalities

occasional.notes: Abnormal connection between urethra and skin or other organs

rare.notes: Failure of normal separation of urinary and genital tracts
searchTerms: abnormal urinary and genital tract connection

laboratory: Urinalysis showing recurrent infections or hematuria
Serum creatinine and blood urea nitrogen to assess renal function
imaging: Ultrasound demonstrating hydronephrosis or structural abnormalities
Voiding cystourethrogram (VCUG) to detect vesicoureteral reflux
MRI or CT urography for detailed anatomical assessment
genetic: Mutations in genes involved in urogenital development such as WT1, PAX2, or HNF1B
other: Endoscopic evaluation of urethra and bladder

distinguishingFeatures: Usually presents with bladder distension and severe obstruction in males
Absence or hypoplasia of uterus and upper vagina
Normal external genitalia and normal ovarian function

redFlags: Severe urinary obstruction causing renal impairment
references: National Organization for Rare Disorders (NORD) - Urogenital Malformations
UpToDate: Congenital anomalies of the urinary tract
